messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] SPDE binomial gives negative fitted values
parts:
this is discussed in the 'short tutorial' vignette, see attached.

with one 'family', then you need to add

control.predictor=list(link=1)


On Thu, 2021-11-04 at 14:19 -0700, anik.panne...@gmail.com wrote:
> Hi,
> I am trying to run an spde model with a covariate. The response is
> binomial.
> I am able to run the model without problem, but the fitted values are
> negative.
>  
> Here is the code :
> AB.sp2 is a SpatialPointsDataFrame with the data and pred2 is a
> dataframe containing the prediction points (regular grid over the
> study area).
>  
> coo <- cbind(AB.sp2$lon/1000, AB.sp2$lat/1000) # units in km
> pcAB <- AB.sp2@data
> mesh <- inla.mesh.2d(loc = coo, max.edge = c(20,60), cutoff = 0.1)
> spde <- inla.spde2.pcmatern(mesh = mesh, prior.range=c(1000,0.001),
> prior.sigma=c(10,0.1)) # I put a really high value for the range prior
> otherwise it seemed to overfit the data
> indexs <- inla.spde.make.index("s", spde$n.spde)
> A <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh = mesh, loc = coo)
> stk.e <- inla.stack(
>   tag = "est",
>   data = list(y = pcAB$claim, numtrials = pcAB$EEdays),
>   A = list(1, A),
>   effects = list(data.frame(b0 = rep(1,nrow(pcAB)), rms = pcAB$rms10),
> s = indexs)
> )
>  
>  
> coop <- cbind(pred2$lon/1000, pred2$lat/1000) # units in km
> Ap <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh = mesh, loc = coop)
> stk.p <- inla.stack(
>   tag = "pred",
>   data = list(y = NA, numtrials = NA),
>   A = list(1, Ap),
>   effects = list(data.frame(b0 = rep(1,nrow(pred2)), rms =
> pred2$rms10), s = indexs)
> )
>  
>  
> stk.full <- inla.stack(stk.e, stk.p)
>  
> formula <- y ~ 0 + b0 + rms + f(s, model = spde)
>  
> res <- inla(formula,
>             family = "binomial",
>             Ntrials = numtrials,
>             data = inla.stack.data(stk.full),
>             control.predictor = list(
>               compute = TRUE, link = 1,
>               A = inla.stack.A(stk.full)),
>             num.threads = 16,
>             verbose = TRUE,
>             control.inla =list(strategy ="adaptive", int.strategy
> ="eb"),
>             inla.mode ="experimental"
> )
>  
> I tried adding   “control.inla =list(strategy ="adaptive",
> int.strategy ="eb")” and  “ inla.mode ="experimental"” to make the
> model run faster.
> Then I run
> index <- inla.stack.index(stk.full, tag = "pred")$data
> pred_mean <- res$summary.fitted.values[index, "mean"]
>  
> And I get :
> summary(pred_mean)
> Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max.
> -13.134 -11.593 -11.474 -11.119 -10.824  -7.279
>  
> Maybe I am mistaken, but I thought that the predictions values should
> be only positive values for a binomial.
>  
> Did I do something wrong ?
>  
> I know that the “success” rate in my data is really low : only around
> 1.7% of the observations have a “success” (thus a response of 1).
> Could that be the problem ? If so, is there anything I can do to fix
> it ?
>  
> Thanks a lot
> Anik
